groups.title: Phase 4 · Live demo v1: Compose on one VPS
Phase 6 · Terraform and your own AWS account
Phase 8 · Live demo v2: 3-node k3s + GitOps

tasks.title: Confirm the freeze point
tasks.how: in ~/Desktop/All_In_One/DevOps run git status, git log --oneline -5 and git tag --list 'app-v*'; note the tag in ENGINEERING_LOG.md.
tasks.done: main is clean and tagged. From now on the app changes only through PRs.

tasks.title: Rebuild the Linux VM
tasks.how: free the Mac to ≥ 100 GB of disk; create a fresh Ubuntu 24.04 LTS ARM64 VM in Parallels (6 vCPU, 10–12 GB RAM, 80 GB disk); connect with VS Code Remote-SSH; delete the 23.04 VM once the new one works.
tasks.done: lsb_release -a shows 24.04 and you can SSH in with a key.

tasks.title: Install the toolchain in the VM
tasks.how: from each tool's official repository or release page: Docker Engine + buildx + compose plugin, kubectl, k3d, Helm, k9s, Terraform, AWS CLI, Azure CLI, ArgoCD CLI, k6, gitleaks, pre-commit, Trivy, hadolint, shellcheck, jq and yq. Add your user to the docker group.
tasks.done: every --version works and the versions are listed in ENGINEERING_LOG.md.

tasks.title: Domain and Cloudflare
tasks.how: create a Cloudflare account; buy the domain at Cloudflare Registrar (at-cost price, and the DNS is already on Cloudflare); turn on DNSSEC.
tasks.done: the zone shows "Active" in Cloudflare.

tasks.title: Open the other accounts
tasks.how: OVHcloud (identity and card checks can take a day or two), Tailscale and healthchecks.io (§5).
tasks.done: you can log in to each one.

tasks.title: Learn how Folionix runs
tasks.how: read Learning Guide Parts 1–4, 5.10–5.11 and 12–16; run make deps && make dev; open the app, /api/docs/, Mailpit and the MinIO console; run make test and make e2e.
tasks.done: you can explain, without notes, what each of the 11 processes does and how one upload flows through the system (Learning Guide 1.3).

tasks.title: Write the service inventory
tasks.how: in ENGINEERING_LOG.md, one table row per process: image, command, port, env vars (from .env.example), health endpoints, dependencies, the data it keeps, stateless or stateful.
tasks.done: all 11 processes are covered. This table is the source for every Dockerfile, Compose service and Kubernetes manifest you write.

tasks.title: Create the GitHub org and repos
tasks.how: create the org folionix and require 2FA for members. First scan the app's full history with gitleaks git (older versions: gitleaks detect): it must report no leaks. Then push the app to folionix/app and create folionix/platform with the folder layout in spec §B7 and a README.
tasks.done: both repos exist and the history scan was clean.

tasks.title: Guard rails on both repos
tasks.how: pre-commit with gitleaks, trailing-whitespace, end-of-file and YAML lint (later add hadolint, terraform fmt and shellcheck); GitHub secret scanning with push protection (free on public repos); Dependabot alerts; a ruleset on main: PR required, no force-push, linear history (required checks come in F-23); CODEOWNERS as in spec §B8 (0 required approvals while you are the only maintainer).
tasks.done: a direct push to main is rejected and the hook blocks a commit containing a fake token.

tasks.title: Ops scripts (platform/scripts/)
tasks.how: healthcheck.sh calls every health endpoint, prints a table and exits non-zero on any failure; pg-backup.sh runs pg_dump -Fc to a timestamped file; pg-restore.sh restores into a scratch database and counts rows in the key tables; disk-cleanup.sh. All of them pass shellcheck.
tasks.done: a backup → restore round trip shows identical row counts.

tasks.title: Architecture diagram
tasks.how: in Excalidraw or draw.io, from the F-07 table: browser → frontend → core-api → search-svc / ai-svc, plus Postgres, Redis, object storage and Meilisearch, with ports. Keep the source file and a PNG in docs/.
tasks.done: someone else can follow a request through it.

tasks.title: 12-factor audit
tasks.how: check config, logs, processes, backing services, disposability and dev/prod parity against the app; record what you find; open app issues for real gaps.
tasks.done: the audit is in ENGINEERING_LOG.md.

tasks.title: Dockerfile for core-api and worker (one image)
tasks.how: multi-stage: install dependencies with uv in a builder stage, then copy only the virtualenv and the code into a slim Python 3.13 runtime; a pinned base image tag and a .dockerignore (no .git, .venv, node_modules, .env or test output); runs as a non-root user with a fixed UID; no compilers or build tools in the final image; one image, two commands: web (gunicorn with uvicorn workers) and worker (celery). Migrations are not in the entrypoint: they run as a one-off command; PYTHONUNBUFFERED=1 and logs to stdout; decide how Django's static files are served (check settings.py, Learning Guide 5.1)
tasks.done: hadolint is clean, the image is under ~300 MB, and docker run with an env file answers /healthz.

tasks.title: Dockerfiles for search-svc and ai-svc
tasks.how: the same rules, with a uvicorn entrypoint.
tasks.done: both answer their health endpoints from a container.

tasks.title: Dockerfile for the frontend
tasks.how: a Node build stage, then an unprivileged nginx image serving the built files; SPA fallback to index.html; long cache headers for hashed assets and no cache for index.html; runtime config injected when the container starts, so one image works in every environment; /api proxied to core-api so the browser stays on one origin.
tasks.done: the same image works with two different API settings without a rebuild.

tasks.title: compose.yaml
tasks.how: every process from F-07; a healthcheck on each service plus depends_on with condition: service_healthy; named volumes for Postgres, MinIO and Meilisearch; a one-off migrate service (or docker compose run --rm for migrations); a one-off bucket-setup job that also sets the CORS rule; Ollama only under profiles: [ai]; memory limits; secrets from a git-ignored .env (commit only .env.example).
tasks.done: docker compose up -d from a fresh clone brings everything to healthy.

tasks.title: Seed, reset and repair in containers
tasks.how: make seed-quick, restore-snapshot, reconcile and replay-dlq work against the containers (Make targets that call docker compose run --rm …).
tasks.done: the golden snapshot restores into the Compose stack.

tasks.title: Multi-arch images
tasks.how: docker buildx create --use, then build with --platform linux/amd64,linux/arm64; check with docker buildx imagetools inspect on each image.
tasks.done: every image lists both platforms.

tasks.title: Prove it
tasks.how: run the Playwright smoke test and make k6-smoke against the containers; scan each image with trivy image --severity CRITICAL --ignore-unfixed.
tasks.done: the tests pass and no critical CVEs are left.

tasks.title: Docker in depth
tasks.how: exec-form entrypoints so the app is PID 1 (or docker run --init / tini); STOPSIGNAL and stop_grace_period so Celery finishes its task; BuildKit cache mounts for uv and npm, and --mount=type=secret for any build-time token (never ARG or ENV); compare slim and distroless for one service (size, CVEs, how you debug it); inspect layers with docker history and dive; a compose.override.yaml for development (bind mounts, hot reload) separate from the production file; network drivers (bridge, host, none) and how Compose DNS works; limits for CPU, memory and PIDs, watched with docker stats; debugging with logs, exec, inspect, events, cp and nicolaka/netshoot attached with --network container:<name>.
tasks.done: docker stop on the worker finishes the running task inside the grace period, you can explain every layer of the core-api image, and you have done drills P-58 to P-62.

tasks.title: pr.yml (spec §D1)
tasks.how: on pull_request: lint (ruff, eslint) → unit tests with Postgres and Redis service containers → multi-arch build without pushing → Trivy (fail on critical) → gitleaks → the Playwright smoke test against Compose on the runner. Read-only permissions and no secrets; dependency and buildx caching; superseded runs cancelled.
tasks.done: a PR shows every check green in under ~15 minutes.

tasks.title: release.yml
tasks.how: on pushes to main and tags v*: build both platforms (tip: amd64 on ubuntu-24.04 and arm64 natively on the free ubuntu-24.04-arm runner, then merge the manifests) → Trivy → push to ghcr.io/folionix/* tagged with the short commit SHA (plus the version on tags). Never deploy latest.
tasks.done: merging to main produces images for both platforms in GHCR.

tasks.title: Supply-chain hygiene
tasks.how: pin third-party actions to a commit SHA; Dependabot or Renovate for pip, npm, Docker base images and GitHub Actions (weekly); a scheduled weekly Trivy scan of the deployed tags.
tasks.done: the first dependency PR arrives and passes CI.

tasks.title: Make the checks required
tasks.how: add the pr.yml jobs as required status checks in the main ruleset.
tasks.done: a PR with a failing test cannot be merged.

tasks.title: Code, app and IaC scanning
tasks.how: CodeQL (free on public repos) or Semgrep for Python and TypeScript; an OWASP ZAP baseline scan against the Compose stack in CI (report only at first, then fail on high findings); Checkov or trivy config on Dockerfiles and compose now, Terraform and Helm later; a SECURITY.md.
tasks.done: a PR that adds an SQL-injection pattern is blocked (P-80), and every run attaches the ZAP report.

tasks.title: Order and harden the server
tasks.how: order one OVHcloud VPS-3 with Ubuntu 24.04 (§5). Create a sudo user; SSH keys only (PasswordAuthentication no, PermitRootLogin no); unattended-upgrades; time zone UTC. Install Tailscale and SSH only over Tailscale, then close port 22 to the internet (OVH Edge Network Firewall plus ufw default deny incoming).
tasks.done: a port scan from outside finds nothing open and you can still SSH in over Tailscale.

tasks.title: Docker on the server
tasks.how: Docker Engine and the compose plugin; log rotation in /etc/docker/daemon.json (max-size 10m, max-file 3).
tasks.done: docker run hello-world works and logs rotate.

tasks.title: Cloudflare Tunnel
tasks.how: in Cloudflare Zero Trust create a tunnel; run cloudflared with its token as a Compose service; route demo.<domain> to the frontend container; turn on "Always Use HTTPS".
tasks.done: the demo loads from your phone on mobile data and the server still has no inbound port open.

tasks.title: Object storage for the demo
tasks.how: one private Cloudflare R2 bucket for files and a second for backups; an R2 API token limited to those buckets; a CORS rule for the demo origin (PUT, GET and the headers the upload needs); S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT_URL set to the R2 endpoint.
tasks.done: an upload on the demo reaches done and its thumbnail loads.

tasks.title: Secrets on the server
tasks.how: generate each secret with openssl rand -base64 32 into .env, owned by the deploy user with mode 600; keep a copy in your password manager; never put it in Git.
tasks.done: ls -l .env shows -rw-------.

tasks.title: Deploy and roll back with one command
tasks.how: platform/scripts/deploy.sh takes a tag: it records the current tag as "previous", pulls the images for the new tag, runs migrations as a one-off, runs docker compose up -d, waits until healthy, runs healthcheck.sh and prints the version. To roll back, run it with the previous tag.
tasks.done: you have deployed two versions and rolled back once, with every step in the log.

tasks.title: Demo mode and the nightly reset
tasks.how: DEMO_MODE=true (banner, demo accounts, OTP shown on screen); a systemd timer at 03:00 UTC restores the golden snapshot into the containers and logs the result; the job pings healthchecks.io when it succeeds (P-46).
tasks.done: the reset has run once on its own and its healthchecks.io check is green.

tasks.title: Off-box backups
tasks.how: nightly pg-backup.sh to the R2 backup bucket with a 14-day lifecycle rule; once a week restore the latest dump into a scratch database and compare row counts.
tasks.done: one restore test is in the log.

tasks.title: External status page
tasks.how: Upptime (a free GitHub repo using Actions and Pages) or Gatus on separate infrastructure; check the demo page and the API health endpoint every 5 minutes; publish it at status.<domain>; email alerts. It must never run on the server it watches.
tasks.done: stopping the app turns the status page red within ~10 minutes.

tasks.title: First runbook: "site is down"
tasks.how: docs/runbooks/site-down.md: check the status page → the Cloudflare tunnel health → docker compose ps → logs → disk and memory → restart order → roll back.
tasks.done: you have followed it once in a drill (P-28).

tasks.title: Show it
tasks.how: add the live link, status page and architecture diagram to the README and your portfolio page.
tasks.done: the live link, status page and diagram are on the README and the portfolio page.

tasks.title: Linux troubleshooting toolkit
tasks.how: learn the commands per resource and note them in docs/runbooks/linux-triage.md: CPU and load (uptime, top/htop, pidstat, mpstat), memory (free, vmstat, dmesg for the OOM killer), disk (df -h, df -i, du, iostat -x, lsof +L1), network (ip, ss -tlnp, dig, resolvectl, curl -v, nc, mtr, tcpdump), processes and services (ps, systemctl, journalctl, strace, /proc/<pid>/limits) and TLS (openssl s_client, openssl x509 -noout -dates); learn the USE method and Brendan Gregg's "Linux performance analysis in 60 seconds". Break things on a scratch VM, or on the Compose server at a quiet hour.
tasks.done: the triage runbook exists and you have done P-63 to P-70 at least once each.

tasks.title: Build it by clicking
tasks.how: a VPC with 2 public and 2 private subnets across 2 AZs; an ALB in the public subnets in front of EC2 in the private subnets running the Compose stack; RDS Postgres (private); S3 for files (private, presigned URLs); security groups chained ALB → EC2 → RDS; a CloudWatch alarm on ALB 5xx that emails you through SNS.
tasks.done: the app works through the ALB address.

tasks.title: Document it, then tear it down
tasks.how: docs/aws-manual-build.md with screenshots and the diagram, plus the hourly cost of each piece from the AWS Pricing Calculator; then delete everything.
tasks.done: the document exists: it is the "before" picture for the Terraform version.

tasks.title: Auto Scaling and private-subnet access
tasks.how: a launch template (ARM AMI, user-data that starts the Compose stack, IMDSv2 required, an instance profile); an Auto Scaling group across both private subnets, min 2 / max 4, ALB health checks, target tracking at 50% CPU; a NAT gateway for outbound traffic; no SSH and no bastion: connect with SSM Session Manager; roll out a new launch template version with an instance refresh; a mixed instances policy (Spot + On-Demand) with capacity rebalancing; scheduled and predictive scaling; a lifecycle hook; know placement groups and the EC2 purchase options.
tasks.done: you terminate an instance and the ASG replaces it; a k6 load test scales it out and back in; you open a shell with port 22 closed.

tasks.title: Private networking in depth
tasks.how: an S3 gateway endpoint and interface endpoints for SSM, ECR and Secrets Manager, then remove the NAT gateway and prove the app still works; VPC Flow Logs to CloudWatch Logs; block a port with a NACL and compare it with a security group (stateless vs stateful); peer a second VPC and fix the routes; use Reachability Analyzer once; make the VPC dual-stack (IPv6) and note the public IPv4 charge it avoids; learn when to use Transit Gateway, PrivateLink, Site-to-Site VPN and Direct Connect.
tasks.done: EC2 reaches S3 with no NAT gateway; a flow log shows a REJECT you caused; you can draw the peering routes from memory.

tasks.title: Storage and data protection
tasks.how: S3 versioning, Block Public Access, a bucket policy that denies non-TLS requests, a lifecycle rule (Standard → Standard-IA after 30 days → Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 90; expire old versions), cross-region replication to a second bucket; a gp3 EBS volume, a snapshot and a restore; an AWS Backup plan for EC2 and RDS; RDS automated backups with a point-in-time restore to a new instance, and a read replica; EFS mounted on two instances.
tasks.done: you restore a deleted S3 object from its old version, and a point-in-time restore holds the data from 5 minutes before you dropped a table.

tasks.title: Secrets, encryption and least privilege
tasks.how: a customer-managed KMS key (read its key policy) used for S3 SSE-KMS, EBS and RDS; the database password in Secrets Manager with rotation on; non-secret settings in SSM Parameter Store; an instance role that can read only its own secret and bucket (no *); check it with the IAM policy simulator and IAM Access Analyzer; a permissions boundary on a test role.
tasks.done: no password appears in user-data, launch templates or env files, and any request outside the role's scope gets AccessDenied.

tasks.title: Event-driven and serverless
tasks.how: S3 upload → event notification (or EventBridge) → SQS queue with a dead-letter queue → a Lambda that reads the file's metadata and writes it to DynamoDB; an SNS topic that fans out to two SQS queues; an API Gateway HTTP API in front of a Lambda that reads from DynamoDB; Lambda logs and metrics in CloudWatch; a Step Functions state machine that chains two Lambdas with a retry.
tasks.done: an upload creates an item in DynamoDB, a bad file lands in the DLQ after 3 tries, and the API returns the item.

tasks.title: DNS, TLS and the edge
tasks.how: delegate a subdomain (aws.folionix.dev) from Cloudflare to a Route 53 hosted zone with NS records; an ACM certificate validated by DNS; an HTTPS listener on the ALB with an HTTP → HTTPS redirect; CloudFront in front of the frontend in S3 (origin access control), with /api/* routed to the ALB; a Route 53 health check with a failover record, plus a weighted record (90/10); AWS WAF on CloudFront with the managed core rule set and a rate limit; know Global Accelerator, S3 Transfer Acceleration and Shield Advanced and when each is worth it.
tasks.done: https://aws.folionix.dev serves the app through CloudFront, the bucket is not public, and a k6 burst is blocked by the rate-limit rule.

tasks.title: Containers without Kubernetes (ECS on Fargate)
tasks.how: push images to ECR (scan on push, a lifecycle policy); an ECS cluster with a Fargate service for core-api behind the ALB; the task role vs the execution role; secrets injected from Secrets Manager; logs to CloudWatch; service auto scaling; rolling deploys with the deployment circuit breaker.
tasks.done: a deploy with a broken image rolls back automatically, and you can explain when you would pick ECS over EKS.

tasks.title: Monitoring and audit on AWS
tasks.how: the CloudWatch agent sends app logs and memory metrics; Logs Insights queries for the top errors and p95 latency; a metric filter on ERROR → alarm → SNS email; a composite alarm; a CloudWatch dashboard; a CloudTrail trail to S3 and an Athena query that finds who deleted a resource; AWS Config with two managed rules (encrypted volumes, no public S3 buckets).
tasks.done: you can answer "who changed this security group, and when?" from CloudTrail in under 5 minutes.

tasks.title: Migrating to AWS
tasks.how: move the demo database from the VPS into RDS with AWS DMS (full load + ongoing replication, then a cutover) and the files into S3 with aws s3 sync (S3 Batch Operations by name); measure the downtime; know the 7 Rs of migration, Application Migration Service, DataSync, Storage Gateway, Transfer Family and the Snow family.
tasks.done: the app runs on RDS with the copied data, the write-up states the cutover downtime, and you can say which migration tool fits which case.

tasks.title: Users, logs and security services
tasks.how: a Cognito user pool with the hosted UI protecting an admin path through the ALB's authenticate action; ALB and WAF logs streamed by Amazon Data Firehose to S3, catalogued by a Glue crawler and queried in Athena (top IPs, 5xx by path); Amazon Inspector scanning ECR images and EC2; Macie run once on the uploads bucket; S3 Object Lock and AWS Backup Vault Lock against ransomware; IAM Access Analyzer unused-access findings.
tasks.done: the admin path asks for a Cognito login, an Athena query lists the top 5xx paths, and Inspector findings match your Trivy results.

tasks.title: Secure the AWS account
tasks.how: root MFA and no root access keys; an IAM Identity Center (or IAM) admin user with MFA for daily work; AWS Budgets at $20/month (alerts at 50%, 80% and 100% actual, and 100% forecast: alerts only warn you; they don't stop charges, and billing data can lag by a day); Cost Anomaly Detection; one EU region for everything.
tasks.done: a test budget alert reaches your inbox.

tasks.title: Bootstrap (terraform/envs/bootstrap)
tasks.how: the state bucket (versioning, encryption, public access blocked, prevent_destroy); every backend uses use_lockfile = true; the GitHub OIDC provider; a read-only plan role trusted for pull requests (repo:folionix/platform:pull_request) and an apply role trusted only for repo:folionix/platform:ref:refs/heads/main.
tasks.done: terraform plan runs in CI with no stored AWS keys.

tasks.title: Modules and the dev environment
tasks.how: modules network (no NAT gateway in dev: one costs ~$35–40/month), database (RDS Postgres db.t4g.micro, private), compute (ARM EC2 running the Compose stack from user-data, behind an ALB) and storage (S3); terraform/envs/dev wires them together with default_tags (project, env, owner, expires).
tasks.done: apply builds the Step 9 setup and the app answers through the ALB.

tasks.title: make cloud-up and make cloud-down
tasks.how: cloud-down destroys the environment, then lists anything chargeable still tagged project=folionix (NAT gateways, load balancers, unattached EBS volumes, Elastic IPs, RDS instances and snapshots, EKS clusters) and exits non-zero if it finds any.
tasks.done: the spec §C4 completion test passes: up → tags visible → down → zero leftovers.

tasks.title: Terraform in CI
tasks.how: on every PR run terraform fmt -check, validate, tflint and trivy config, then post the plan as a PR comment; apply only through a manual workflow with environment approval.
tasks.done: a PR shows its plan as a comment.

tasks.title: The demo as code (terraform/envs/demo)
tasks.how: bring what you can under Terraform with import blocks: Cloudflare DNS records and tunnel routes (Cloudflare provider) and, if the ovh provider can import your VPS, the server too; everything else goes into a bootstrap script in platform/scripts/.
tasks.done: plan shows no changes.

tasks.title: Drill S-3 (P-26)
tasks.how: drift, import and a stuck lock, as described in §4.
tasks.done: the write-up is in docs/scenarios/.

tasks.title: Multi-account and security baseline
tasks.how: AWS Organizations with management, dev and prod (or sandbox) accounts; IAM Identity Center for logging in to each; SCPs that deny regions outside your EU region, leaving the organization and stopping CloudTrail; an organization CloudTrail; GuardDuty, Security Hub and IAM Access Analyzer turned on (note when each free trial ends and switch off what you do not keep); cost allocation tags activated.
tasks.done: launching EC2 in us-east-1 from the dev account is denied by the SCP, and a GuardDuty sample finding reaches your email.

tasks.title: Terraform the extras
tasks.how: modules for everything from F-36a–h (asg, endpoints, kms, secrets, dns + acm, cdn + waf, events: sqs/lambda/dynamodb, ecs); the Lambda packaged in CI; Checkov in CI; terraform test for one module.
tasks.done: make cloud-up builds the full F-36 setup and make cloud-down leaves nothing behind.

tasks.title: Deploy to AWS from CI
tasks.how: GitHub Actions with OIDC deploys a new image to ECS (render the task definition → deploy → wait for stability), and the EC2 version through an ASG instance refresh; a manual approval for prod with GitHub environments.
tasks.done: merging to main updates dev, with no AWS keys stored anywhere.

tasks.title: AWS CLI, scripting and cost
tasks.how: everyday CLI with --query and jq; a boto3 script that lists untagged and idle resources (unattached EBS volumes, old snapshots, idle load balancers, unused Elastic IPs); rewrite it during Python Basics; Cost Explorer grouped by tag and by usage type (find NAT and data-transfer charges); know Savings Plans vs Reserved Instances vs Spot, Compute Optimizer and Trusted Advisor.
tasks.done: the script runs weekly in GitHub Actions and posts its findings, and you can explain the three biggest lines on your bill.

tasks.title: Terraform beyond the basics
tasks.how: for_each over maps vs count (and when count is fine); dynamic blocks; locals and validation blocks on variables; sharing outputs between stacks with terraform_remote_state or data sources; refactoring with moved blocks and terraform state mv / rm; lifecycle create_before_destroy, ignore_changes and replace_triggered_by; terraform plan -replace; modules pinned to Git tags; provider pins with a committed .terraform.lock.hcl and Renovate updates; sensitive outputs and keeping secrets out of state (RDS manage_master_user_password); know workspaces vs directories, and Terragrunt and Atlantis by name.
tasks.done: you refactor the network module from count to for_each and the plan shows only moves, no replacements; P-73 to P-76 are written up.

tasks.title: CloudFormation and CDK
tasks.how: build the S3 → SQS → Lambda part once in CloudFormation and once with the CDK (Python); deploy through change sets from CI; stack drift detection, rollback and termination protection; SAM for packaging the Lambda; an ADR comparing them with Terraform.
tasks.done: the stack deploys from CI through a change set, and the ADR says when you would choose each tool.

tasks.title: Cross-account, tracing and automation
tasks.how: cross-account roles (aws sts assume-role from dev into a read-only role in prod; CI role chaining); the AWS Distro for OpenTelemetry sending core-api traces to X-Ray; a CloudWatch Synthetics canary on the login page; AWS Health events → EventBridge → SNS; EventBridge Scheduler stopping dev EC2 and RDS every night.
tasks.done: you can follow one slow request in X-Ray, the canary alarms when login breaks, and dev stops itself at night.

tasks.title: Local cluster
tasks.how: k3d cluster create folionix --agents 2 -p "8080:80@loadbalancer"; namespaces folionix and monitoring.
tasks.done: kubectl get nodes shows 3 Ready nodes.

tasks.title: Plain manifests
tasks.how: Deployments (core-api ×2, worker, search-svc, ai-svc at 0 replicas, frontend ×2), ClusterIP Services and an Ingress for the frontend and /api; ConfigMaps for settings; Secrets created with kubectl create secret generic … --from-env-file (never committed); StatefulSets with PVCs for Postgres and Meilisearch; Redis with append-only persistence.
tasks.done: the app works at http://localhost:8080.

tasks.title: Make the pods production-grade
tasks.how: a startupProbe for Django's slow start, readinessProbe → /readyz, livenessProbe → /healthz only (never check the database in liveness, P-14); requests and limits from measured kubectl top values; a securityContext (runAsNonRoot, readOnlyRootFilesystem where possible, drop ALL capabilities, no privilege escalation); PodDisruptionBudgets and topology spread for core-api and frontend; the namespace label pod-security.kubernetes.io/enforce=restricted.
tasks.done: the restricted Pod Security level admits every pod.

tasks.title: Jobs
tasks.how: migrations as a Job (later a Helm pre-upgrade hook); seed and snapshot restore as Jobs.
tasks.done: a fresh cluster goes from empty to seeded using Jobs only.

tasks.title: Drill S-9: NetworkPolicies
tasks.how: default-deny ingress and egress in folionix; allow DNS to kube-dns on UDP/TCP 53 first (P-16); then allow only the paths in your diagram; test each with kubectl exec … -- nc -zv <service> <port>.
tasks.done: ai-svc → Postgres is blocked and everything else works; recorded.

tasks.title: RBAC, quotas and Pod Security
tasks.how: one ServiceAccount per workload, with automountServiceAccountToken: false where the API is not needed; a namespaced Role for a "developer" (read pods and logs, exec in folionix only) and a read-only role for CI checks; check them with kubectl auth can-i --list --as=…; a user with a client certificate (CKA style), and how OIDC users work on EKS and AKS; a ResourceQuota and a LimitRange on folionix; the Pod Security Admission label restricted on folionix.
tasks.done: the developer can read logs but cannot read Secrets or delete Deployments, and a pod without requests gets the LimitRange defaults.

tasks.title: Helm chart (helm/folionix)
tasks.how: templates for every service; values-dev.yaml, values-demo.yaml and values-prod.yaml; a values.schema.json; helm lint plus helm template | kubeconform -strict in platform CI; upgrades with --rollback-on-failure (Helm 4; --atomic in Helm 3), --wait and --timeout 10m.
tasks.done: helm install on a fresh k3d cluster brings up the whole app and Playwright passes against it.

tasks.title: Kustomize
tasks.how: a base and overlays (dev, demo) for one service or for the platform add-ons; patches, configMapGenerator and the images transformer; sync it with ArgoCD; an ADR on when you use Helm and when Kustomize.
tasks.done: kubectl kustomize overlays/demo renders cleanly and ArgoCD syncs it.

tasks.title: Autoscaling
tasks.how: an HPA on core-api (CPU 70% to start); load it with k6 browse.js; watch kubectl get hpa -w.
tasks.done: replicas rise under load and fall back afterwards.

tasks.title: CronJobs
tasks.how: the nightly demo reset and a nightly pg_dump to object storage (the start of S-24), with concurrencyPolicy: Forbid, startingDeadlineSeconds and history limits.
tasks.done: both run on schedule and failures show in kubectl get jobs.

tasks.title: CKA side task
tasks.how: on a 3-VM kubeadm cluster (spec §C1), practise an etcd snapshot + restore and a minor-version upgrade.
tasks.done: both are in your notes with the exact commands.

tasks.title: Build the cluster (§5)
tasks.how: order 3 new VPS-3 nodes in the same datacentre (Terraform or the console); keep the Compose server running. Harden each node as in F-24 and open the k3s ports only between the three nodes. Install k3s as an HA cluster with embedded etcd: --cluster-init on the first server and --server https://<node-1>:6443 on the other two, all with --flannel-backend=wireguard-native so pod traffic between nodes is encrypted; turn on etcd snapshots to R2.
tasks.done: kubectl get nodes shows 3 Ready control-plane nodes and an etcd snapshot exists in R2.

tasks.title: ArgoCD
tasks.how: install a minimal ArgoCD; change the admin password and store it; reach the UI only with kubectl port-forward or at argocd.<domain> behind Cloudflare Access (Zero Trust, free): never on the open internet without a login.
tasks.done: the UI asks for Cloudflare Access before the ArgoCD login.

tasks.title: App-of-apps (platform/argocd/)
tasks.how: one root app that creates child apps: sealed-secrets, cloudflared (2 replicas), CloudNativePG and its cluster, kube-prometheus-stack, and folionix (values-demo.yaml); sync waves so operators and CRDs come first; automated sync with prune and selfHeal.
tasks.done: a resource you delete by hand is recreated from Git.

tasks.title: Secrets the GitOps way
tasks.how: install Sealed Secrets; encrypt each secret with kubeseal and commit only the SealedSecret YAML; back up the controller key straight away, encrypted, in your password manager (P-36).
tasks.done: a sealed secret still decrypts after you restart the controller.

tasks.title: A highly available database
tasks.how: a CloudNativePG cluster with 3 instances (one per node, anti-affinity) on local-path volumes; scheduled base backups and WAL archiving to R2.
tasks.done: deleting the primary pod promotes a replica and the app reconnects, and a backup shows up in R2.

tasks.title: Postgres operations
tasks.how: pg_stat_statements on; a slow-query log (log_min_duration_statement = 250ms); EXPLAIN (ANALYZE, BUFFERS) on the three slowest queries; an index added with CREATE INDEX CONCURRENTLY through a Django migration; autovacuum and table bloat basics; lock_timeout and statement_timeout for migrations; PgBouncer through the CloudNativePG Pooler; replication lag and synchronous vs asynchronous replicas; a major-version upgrade (17 → 18) rehearsed on a copy, with timings.
tasks.done: a Grafana panel shows the top queries, the upgrade write-up states the downtime, and P-77 to P-79 are done.

tasks.title: The release flow

tasks.done: one merge in app reaches the live demo with no manual step.

tasks.done: the status page shows no downtime during the switch.

tasks.title: Drill S-1: zero-downtime deploys (P-06)
tasks.how: maxUnavailable 0 and maxSurge 1; readiness on /readyz; a preStop sleep of about 10 s; gunicorn's graceful timeout shorter than terminationGracePeriodSeconds; run k6 during a release.
tasks.done: k6 reports 0% failed requests during the rollout; recorded.

tasks.title: Update the runbooks for Kubernetes

tasks.title: kube-prometheus-stack
tasks.how: through ArgoCD, with demo-sized values: 7-day retention, a 10 GB volume, a 30 s scrape interval; Grafana with an anonymous read-only viewer at grafana.<domain>; admin access only behind Cloudflare Access.
tasks.done: the public dashboard loads with no login and the admin page asks for Cloudflare Access.

tasks.title: ImagePullBackOff
tasks.how: set a tag that doesn't exist, or make a GHCR package private with no pull secret.

tasks.title: CrashLoopBackOff from bad config
tasks.how: remove DATABASE_URL from the Secret, or set a wrong password.

tasks.title: OOMKilled (S-8)
tasks.how: turn on the memory-leak chaos switch, or set the worker's memory limit to 128Mi and upload a large PDF.

tasks.title: A pod is stuck Pending
tasks.how: request memory: 64Gi, use a StorageClass that doesn't exist, or set a nodeSelector no node matches.

tasks.title: A liveness probe causes a restart storm
tasks.how: point liveness at /readyz (which checks the database) with a 1 s timeout, then run k6 with CHAOS_LATENCY_MS=1500.

tasks.title: The HPA doesn't scale
tasks.how: remove the CPU requests from core-api.

tasks.title: A NetworkPolicy blocks DNS
tasks.how: apply default-deny egress without the DNS rule.

tasks.title: Disk full / DiskPressure
tasks.how: on k3d, fill the Postgres volume with fallocate, or fill the node's disk.

tasks.title: A node dies or is drained
tasks.how: on k3d docker stop k3d-folionix-agent-1; on the demo, kubectl drain a node with --ignore-daemonsets --delete-emptydir-data under k6 load.

tasks.title: Slow at low CPU: throttling
tasks.how: set core-api's CPU limit to 100m and run k6 browse.js.

tasks.title: Pods can't talk across nodes
tasks.how: leave 51820/udp closed between the nodes, or block the pod network (10.42.0.0/16) in ufw.

tasks.title: The backup exists but the restore fails (S-24)
tasks.how: in a test namespace, delete some submissions and their files, then restore from last night's backup.

tasks.title: The database runs out of connections
tasks.how: scale core-api to 8 replicas × 4 workers with persistent connections, lower Postgres max_connections and run k6.

tasks.title: Redis goes down (S-11)
tasks.how: scale Redis to 0 during uploads.

tasks.title: A poison message ends up in the dead-letter queue (S-12)
tasks.how: from a Celery shell, send a task with a malformed payload.

tasks.title: The search index is lost (S-13)
tasks.how: delete the Meilisearch volume.

tasks.title: Terraform: stuck lock, drift, a hand-made resource (S-3)
tasks.how: (a) kill terraform apply half-way; (b) change a security group in the console; (c) create an S3 bucket by hand.

tasks.title: Destroying the wrong thing
tasks.how: try to destroy envs/bootstrap.

tasks.title: Site down: the tunnel is disconnected
tasks.how: scale cloudflared to 0.

tasks.title: 502 Bad Gateway: the tunnel is up, the app is unreachable
tasks.how: point the tunnel route at the wrong port, or scale the frontend to 0.

tasks.title: Uploads fail in the browser (CORS / presigned URL)
tasks.how: delete the bucket's CORS rule, or set S3_PUBLIC_ENDPOINT_URL to an internal hostname.

tasks.title: A DNS record is deleted
tasks.how: delete the demo record in Cloudflare.

tasks.title: An expired certificate (cloud drills with cert-manager)
tasks.how: in a drill, use a broken ClusterIssuer.

tasks.title: A traffic spike or bot abuse
tasks.how: a short k6 run with 200 virtual users against search on your own demo.

tasks.title: An internal endpoint is exposed
tasks.how: add an Ingress path for /metrics.

tasks.title: Containers run as root
tasks.how: remove the securityContext.

tasks.title: CI credentials are too powerful
tasks.how: try terraform apply from a PR branch.

tasks.title: Forgotten resources keep billing
tasks.how: leave the dev environment with a NAT gateway up for 1 hour, then run only the leftover check.

tasks.title: The VPS provider has a problem
tasks.how: pretend one node (or the whole provider) is gone.

tasks.title: Monitoring is down and nobody knows
tasks.how: scale Prometheus and Alertmanager to 0.

tasks.title: Alert noise
tasks.how: alert on CPU > 50% for 1 minute.

tasks.title: Prometheus runs out of memory (high cardinality)
tasks.how: add a label with raw URL paths (IDs included) to a metric, then run k6 over many submissions.

tasks.title: Rebuild from zero (S-15)
tasks.how: destroy the drill cluster (keep the state bucket and backups). Fix now: terraform apply → bootstrap ArgoCD → restore the Sealed Secrets key → sync the root app → restore the database → smoke test; time each step. Prevent: everything in Git; the bootstrap tested monthly; a 30-minute RTO target.

tasks.title: A whole cloud region is lost (S-16)
tasks.how: take the AWS environment down during a drill. Fix now: fail over to Azure with DNS health checks and measure the switch time.

tasks.title: An upgrade removes an API (S-20)
tasks.how: keep a manifest on an API version that the new cluster version removed.

tasks.title: A CronJob fails silently
tasks.how: give the nightly reset a wrong snapshot path.

tasks.title: The ALB returns 502, 503 or 504
tasks.how: (a) set the target group health check path to /nothing; (b) remove the ALB → EC2 rule from the instance security group; (c) set CHAOS_LATENCY_MS above the ALB idle timeout.

tasks.title: A private instance cannot reach the internet
tasks.how: delete the 0.0.0.0/0 route to the NAT gateway from the private route table.

tasks.title: AccessDenied when the policy looks right
tasks.how: add an explicit Deny to the bucket policy, or encrypt the bucket with a KMS key whose key policy does not allow the role.

tasks.title: RDS connection failures and exhausted connections
tasks.how: (a) remove the EC2 → RDS security group rule; (b) run k6 against workers with a pool that never closes connections.

tasks.title: The Auto Scaling group keeps replacing instances
tasks.how: a launch template version with broken user-data (a wrong image tag).

tasks.title: Messages processed twice, or never
tasks.how: set the SQS visibility timeout shorter than the Lambda run time; then upload a file the Lambda cannot parse.

tasks.title: CloudFront 403 and a certificate stuck in "pending validation"
tasks.how: remove the origin access control statement from the bucket policy; request an ACM certificate without creating its DNS record, or in a region other than us-east-1.

tasks.title: EKS pods get no AWS credentials or no IP address
tasks.how: (a) point the service account at a role whose trust policy names another namespace; (b) put the nodes in small /27 subnets and scale up.

tasks.title: A surprise bill
tasks.how: pull images through the NAT gateway in a loop for an hour; leave a large EBS snapshot and an unused Elastic IP.

tasks.title: An access key leaks
tasks.how: create an access key for a test user with no permissions, use it from your Mac, and treat it as leaked. Never push a real key.

tasks.title: An Availability Zone fails
tasks.how: give one AZ's subnets a NACL that denies everything, and force an RDS Multi-AZ failover.

tasks.title: An EC2 instance fails its status checks
tasks.how: fill the root volume, or break /etc/fstab on a test instance and reboot.

tasks.title: Lambda is throttled
tasks.how: set reserved concurrency to 1 and upload 100 files at once.

tasks.title: Route 53 failover does not fail over
tasks.how: point the health check at a path that always returns 200, then stop the primary app.

tasks.title: EKS nodes never join the cluster
tasks.how: create a node group with a role that is missing a policy, or in subnets with no route to the API endpoint.

tasks.title: Files deleted or encrypted (ransomware)
tasks.how: with versioning on, delete a folder of objects in the uploads bucket by script.

tasks.title: A CloudFormation stack is stuck
tasks.how: make an update fail in a way rollback cannot undo (delete a resource by hand first).

tasks.title: Spot capacity disappears
tasks.how: run the ASG on one Spot instance type in one AZ, then simulate an interruption with AWS FIS.

tasks.title: docker stop is slow and work is lost
tasks.how: use a shell-form ENTRYPOINT (sh -c "celery …") so the shell is PID 1.

tasks.title: Permission denied on a volume
tasks.how: run as UID 10001 with a volume created earlier by root.

tasks.title: Containers cannot reach each other
tasks.how: put search-svc on another Compose network, or use localhost in DATABASE_URL.

tasks.title: Docker fills the disk
tasks.how: build many times without pruning; run one container without log rotation.

tasks.title: Slow builds and huge images
tasks.how: COPY . . before installing dependencies; leave build tools in the final stage.

tasks.title: The server is slow: CPU or I/O?
tasks.how: stress-ng --cpu 6, then a heavy fio write in a scratch directory.

tasks.title: "No space left" while df shows free space
tasks.how: create a million tiny files; delete a large log that a process still holds open.

tasks.title: Too many open files
tasks.how: set LimitNOFILE=256 for a service and run k6.

tasks.title: A systemd service will not start
tasks.how: put a typo in a unit, or make its env file unreadable.

tasks.title: DNS fails on the host
tasks.how: break /etc/resolv.conf or the systemd-resolved stub.

tasks.title: Connection refused or timed out?
tasks.how: bind a service to 127.0.0.1; separately, block its port in ufw.

tasks.title: TLS handshake errors
tasks.how: serve an expired certificate or one without its intermediate on a test nginx; call it with the wrong SNI.

tasks.title: The host runs out of memory
tasks.how: stress-ng --vm on a node with no limits.

tasks.title: Forbidden (RBAC)
tasks.how: give the CI ServiceAccount only the view role and let it try to deploy.

tasks.title: A quota blocks a deploy
tasks.how: a ResourceQuota of 2 CPUs on the namespace, then scale up.

tasks.title: Removing one item destroys many (count)
tasks.how: create subnets with count over a list, then remove the first item.

tasks.title: Renaming a resource destroys it
tasks.how: rename aws_db_instance.main to .primary.

tasks.title: A provider upgrade breaks the plan
tasks.how: bump the AWS or azurerm provider by one major version.

tasks.title: A secret sits in the state file
tasks.how: pass the database password to RDS as a variable, then read the state.

tasks.title: A slow query takes the site down
tasks.how: in a branch migration, drop an index browse depends on; run k6.

tasks.title: A long transaction blocks a migration
tasks.how: hold a row lock in an open psql session, then run a migration that alters the table.

tasks.title: Replica lag and lost writes on failover
tasks.how: run k6 upload_burst.js and kill the primary while replicas are asynchronous.

tasks.title: A scanner blocks the PR
tasks.how: add an endpoint that builds SQL with string formatting.

tasks.title: An NSG blocks traffic
tasks.how: add a deny rule above the allow on the app subnet.

tasks.title: AuthorizationFailed
tasks.how: assign a role at the wrong scope, or test before the assignment has propagated.

tasks.title: Key Vault access denied
tasks.how: remove the managed identity's Key Vault Secrets User role, or turn the vault firewall on.

tasks.title: AKS cannot pull from ACR (optional)
tasks.how: detach ACR, or remove the kubelet identity's AcrPull role.

tasks.title: A private endpoint resolves to a public IP (optional)
tasks.how: delete the private DNS zone link to the VNet.

tasks.title: Application Gateway returns 502 (optional)
tasks.how: break the backend health probe path or the backend port.

tasks.title: Azure Policy denies a deployment (optional)
tasks.how: apply a resource without the required tags.

tasks.title: An Azure surprise bill (optional)
tasks.how: leave Application Gateway, a public IP and a VM disk running overnight.

tasks.title: A commit is lost
tasks.how: git reset --hard HEAD~3 on a branch with unpushed work.

tasks.title: A bad merge breaks main
tasks.how: merge a branch that breaks a test, then add commits on top.

tasks.title: A secret is in Git history
tasks.how: commit a fake key, then remove it in a later commit.

tasks.title: Nginx returns 413, 502 or 504
tasks.how: upload a large PDF with the default body size; stop the upstream; make the upstream slower than the proxy timeout.
